nodes.title: Entry profile update = true and entry identify ≠ true?
nodes.comment: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Entry. Every activation starts clean and takes one of three roads (contract v2): the phone-number change alone (E11), the car alone for a caller who is already identified, or the full pass. What the supervisor passed is copied into the working fields first; the name the caller gave earlier (caller_name) and a safety note are kept as they came. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

nodes.title: Change marked
nodes.comment: E11 (contract v2): the supervisor passed entry_profile_update and it is the only marker that is true, so this entry is the phone-number change and nothing else. The marker is consumed here, so a later entry for another reason does not find it. The status the supervisor holds is the one to start from, and the one that goes back if the change ends with a person: a profile change says nothing about a car, so it never takes an identity away.

nodes.title: Entry identify = true and entry profile update ≠ true?
nodes.comment: Contract v2, section 1: a marker is acted on only when it is the only one that is true. Only entry_identify: the task is the gate (who is calling, and which car). The marker is consumed here, and entry_trusted records that the supervisor named this task.

nodes.title: Entry unmarked
nodes.comment: Both markers true, or neither: they say nothing about this entry (values that reached this agent without being passed for it, or an entry that carried none). Both are put back and the task is worked out as it was before markers existed: from the identity the supervisor holds (entry_known_gate), with a request to change the phone number picked up by the first question that is asked (number_change_wanted, then change_asked). On such an entry no car is settled without a question (single_car_gate), so the request is always read by a speaking step before this agent finishes.

nodes.title: Hint ask
nodes.detail: More than one customer shares this phone number. Without saying so, ask for the caller's full name or the plate number of their car, in one short question. {{#if hint_tries}}What …
nodes.comment: How the speaking steps (REASONING: true) work, here and below. Each asks one thing in the caller's language and stores the answer; the scripted steps around it do every lookup, every count and every decision. A speaking step ends when its outcome field is stored, or when the caller raised a safety problem, asked for a person, or asked to change the phone number on their profile (E11). Its only listed tool is kept closed by a CONSTRAINTS rule, so it cannot call a business tool. MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds caller turns that end without a result; the exact counts of the use cases (E55) are kept by counters in scripted steps. E08: asks the name or a plate to tell the profiles apart.

nodes.title: Car find
nodes.comment: Establishes the facts about the car: spec region, ownership type, where it was sold and the state of its record. The booking specialist applies the eligibility rules. Tool library v2: the lookup stages what it found in found_* and writes none of the contract variables. They are written in car_accept_own, car_accept_other and car_plate_only: after the caller confirmed the plate, and only for a record that can be used. E07: a plate that belongs to a car of another brand is not used. N15: a record marked wrong or exported is not used.
